articles.headline: Chargers TE David Njoku leaves game with knee injury
articles.description: Chargers tight end David Njoku exited Sunday's game against the Raiders in the second quarter on a medical cart with an injury to his right knee.
articles.headlineJa: チャージャーズのTEデビッド・ニョーク、膝の負傷で負傷退場
articles.descriptionJa: チャージャーズのタイトエンド（TE）デビッド・ニョークは、日曜日のレイダース戦の第2クォーターで右膝を負傷し、医療用カートに乗せられて退場しました。
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku exited Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter on a medical cart with an injury to his right knee.

The Chargers officially listed Njoku as questionable to return.

Njoku appeared to get injured while blocking for running back Omarion Hampton. The entire team came out on the field to give Njoku well wishes as he exited.

It wasn't the only Chargers injury on the day, as safety Derwin James exited the game in the first quarter with a hand injury. In his absence, the Chargers allowed a 40-yard touchdown to wide receiver Tre Tucker. The Chargers said James was questionable to return.

The Chargers signed Njoku to a one-year deal in May after he spent his first nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns.

With Njoku out, the Chargers will lean on tight ends Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. Patrick Herbert, a practice squad player who is the brother of quarterback Justin Herbert, could also see time if Njoku's injury is long term.

Njoku had six receptions for 67 yards through two games with the Chargers.

articles.headline: Paris Saint-Germain down Marseille in Le Classique, Timothy Weah sent of
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain closed out a tense 2-1 win over Le Classique rivals Marseille, who finished with 10 men at Stade Velodrome.
articles.headlineJa: パリ・サンジェルマンがル・クラシコでマルセイユを破る、ティモシー・ウェアは退場
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンは、スタッド・ヴェロドロームで行われたライバルのマルセイユとの白熱したル・クラシコを2-1で制しました。マルセイユは10人で試合を終えることとなりました。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain closed out a tense 2-1 win over Le Classique rivals Marseille, who finished with 10 men at Stade Velodrome.

Substitute Ferran Torres headed PSG in front after 66 minutes, but Angel Gomes soon equalised for the home side.

PSG responded almost immediately when captain Marquinhos fired in from a corner to put them back in front with 16 minutes left before Marseille captain Timothy Weah was sent off for a second caution.

Despite the hostile welcome, PSG made a positive start as Fabian Ruiz's flick on found Ousmane Dembélé, who sent an attempted lob over Marseille keeper Jeffrey de Lange which dropped onto the roof of the net.

Marseille sparked into life after 24 minutes when Pierre-Emile Højbjerg saw his 20-yard effort fly straight at PSG keeper Matvey Safonov.

The home side were then forced into an early change when winger Igor Paixão landed awkwardly as he jumped with Warren Zaïre-Emery, and following treatment went off to be replaced by Gomes on the half-hour.

Neal Maupay then sent a left-foot shot from the centre of the box just wide before Gomes blasted his effort over.

PSG -- who have started the 2026-27 campaign sluggishly, failing to win any of their opening three league games before edging past Brest last weekend -- regrouped ahead of half-time.

Zaïre-Emery nodded a cross from the left by Désiré Doué just wide before Dembele sent a rising drive from outside the box over.

PSG were soon on the front foot again early in the second half as Joao Neves' header was saved before Khvicha Kvaratskhelia saw his shot deflected just wide.

Nuno Mendes found Dembele with a deep cross-field pass, but the French striker slid his shot off target, before Neves planted his header over.

Torres, who had not long replaced Kvaratskhelia on the hour, finally made the breakthrough for PSG in the 66th minute.

Doue swung the ball over from the left and Torres got up to put his header into the top corner from six yards out.

Marseille were soon back on level terms in the 72nd minute.

Højbjerg won possession in the middle and fed Amine Gouiri, who strode forwards and played in Gomes to fire past Safonov from close range.

PSG, though, responded straight away when Marquinhos fired home just two minutes later after his initial effort from a corner had been saved.

Marseille were reduced to 10 men with 15 minutes left when defender Weah collected a second yellow card for pulling back Mendes as Bruno Genesio's side slipped to a fourth league defeat from five games.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第2週：日曜日の試合のポイント、疑問点、ファンタジーの視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの記者がすべての熱戦を振り返り、日曜日に行われた各試合の最も重要な疑問に答えます。第2週から見えてきたポイントはこちらです。
articles.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly WR Darius Cooper.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

PHI-TEN | GB-NYJ

CIN-HOU | MIN-CHI | NO-BAL

CAR-ATL | PIT-NE

Catch up on Thursday's game:

DET-BUF

Philadelphia 24, Tennessee 20

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Eagles

How should we feel about the Eagles after this game? The offensive line was too leaky for the second straight week. The defense had issues suppressing an offense that ranked 31st in total yards (195) in Week 1. And quarterback Jalen Hurts, operating without running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) for much of the game, had two interceptions. Hurts orchestrated a touchdown drive in the final seconds to walk away with a win, but Philly's schedule is only going to get tougher from here.

What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw an interception on the Eagles' opening drive -- his first on a pass thrown into the end zone since Week 10 of 2024 -- and another in the second half. But he bounced back to calmly lead the Eagles downfield in the closing moments before finding Darius Cooper for the game-winner with 14 seconds left. -- Tim McManus

Next game: at Bears (Monday, Sept. 28, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Titans

What does this loss do for the Titans confidence going forward? On paper, this game was lopsided. But both units fed off each other. Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll found a nice groove orchestrating two long scoring drives. The defense had interceptions by Amani Hooker and Marcus Harris that led to 10 points. But this is the kind of game the Titans need to find a way to win. Playing the Eagles closely could give them confidence going forward, but when will these turn to wins?

What to make of the QB performance: Ward seemed like he was comfortable executing Daboll's offense. Both of their touchdowns came via Ward's legs, making him the fifth quarterback in franchise history with two rushing TDs in a game over the last 50 seasons. And Ward's 41-yard pass to Elic Ayomanor was the fourth longest of his career. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

articles.headline: Christian Pulisic starts, gets first Milan goal of 2026 in win
articles.description: AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: クリスチャン・プリシッチが先発、勝利を収めた試合で2026年初のミランでのゴールを記録
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランは日曜日、サン・シーロでレッチェに3-0で勝利し、セリエAでの無敗記録を伸ばしました。
articles.body:
AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.

Christian Pulisic fired Ruben Amorim's side ahead early on before second-half goals from Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira wrapped up the win.

Milan now go into the international break fifth in the standings thanks to their third win of the campaign alongside two draws.

Lecce looked to strike in the opening stages as Joel Monteiro and Ivan Ilic both went close, but Milan took the lead in the 14th minute through Pulisic.

A brilliant piece of skill saw the United States striker coolly bring down Strahinja Pavlovic's cross-field pass with a single touch before moving the ball onto his left foot and firing into the bottom corner.

The goal was Pulisic's first for Milan of the calendar year after his red-hot start to the 2025 campaign came to a screeching halt in 2026. The U.S. star was not selected by Mauricio Pochettino for the squad that will play four friendlies in the upcoming international window.

Mike Maignan was called into action to make the save from Kialonda Gaspar and before the break Milan went close in quick succession as Koni De Winter nodded wide before Pavlovic's effort was stopped by Wladimiro Falcone.

Pervis Estupiñán had a shot blocked after the restart, but Milan doubled their advantage 61 minutes in through Rabiot, who completed a team goal following a quick exchange with Gonçalo Ramos before slotting the ball past Falcone.

Estupinan fired wide as the hosts looked to build on their lead and just moments later Moreira scored their third goal of the evening.

The substitute won the ball just inside Lecce's half and raced down the left flank before cutting into the box, where he evaded the visiting defence and hit a low finish underneath Falcone in the 73rd minute.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Braves clinch NL East title with 4-2 win over Astros
articles.description: — Mike Yastrzemski hit a three-run homer during a four-run sixth inning and the Atlanta Braves clinched the NL East title for the seventh time in nine years with a 4-2 win over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ブレーブスがアストロズに4-2で勝利しナ・リーグ東地区優勝を決める
articles.descriptionJa: マイク・ヤストレムスキーが4得点を挙げた6回に3ランホームランを放ち、アトランタ・ブレーブスは日曜日、ヒューストン・アストロズに4-2で勝利して過去9年間で7度目のナ・リーグ東地区優勝を決めました。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — Mike Yastrzemski hit a three-run homer during a four-run sixth inning and the Atlanta Braves clinched the NL East title for the seventh time in nine years with a 4-2 win over the Houston Astros on Sunday.


              Ozzie Albies tied it at one with an RBI single before Yastrzemski’s homer to right off Bryan King (3-6).


              After finishing 76-86 and missing the playoffs last season, Atlanta bounced back this year under first-year manager Walt Weiss. The Braves are 92-64 and have won at least 90 games for the fifth time in the last eight seasons.


              The Astros’ playoff hopes took a hit after being swept by the Braves. Houston, which has lost seven of its last nine games, entered the day trailing the Rangers by a game in the AL West, but the Astros own the tiebreaker.


              Jose Altuve had a home run in the fourth, Yainer Diaz hit a home run in the eighth, but the Astros left the bases loaded in the first and fifth innings.


              Victor Mederos (5-1) entered with the bases loaded and one out in the fifth and struck out Altuve before inducing a groundout by Diaz to end the inning. Dylan Dodd pitched the ninth for his second save.


              Braves starter Martín Pérez allowed one run on six hits in 4 1/3 innings.


              Houston starter Hunter Brown scattered three hits and struck out 10 over five scoreless innings.


              Up next
              Braves: RHP JR Ritchie (1-3, 5.03 ERA) starts Tuesday in the first game of a three-game series against the Reds at home.


              Astros: RHP Cristian Javier (2-6, 5.31) starts Tuesday against the Mariners in the first game of a two-game series in Seattle.


              ------

articles.headline: Marseille fans bash U.S. owner McCourt's 'Ligue 2 project'
articles.description: Angry Marseille fans displayed banners hostile to the club's American owner, Frank McCourt, ahead of and during their Ligue 1 loss to Paris Saint-Germain on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: マルセイユのファン、米国人オーナー・マコート氏の「リーグ・ドゥ（2部）プロジェクト」を猛批判
articles.descriptionJa: 怒りを募らせたマルセイユのファンは日曜日、リーグ・アンのパリ・サンジェルマン戦の試合前および試合中に、クラブの米国人オーナーであるフランク・マコート氏に敵対する横断幕を掲げました。
articles.body:
Angry Marseille fans displayed banners hostile to the club's American owner, Frank McCourt, ahead of and during their Ligue 1 loss to Paris Saint-Germain on Sunday.

Marseille hosted their bitter rivals at the Stade Velodrome on the back of four consecutive losses in all competitions -- with Sunday's 2-1 loss making it five straight. It's the first time Marseille have ever lost four of their opening five games in a top-flight season.

Fans mocked the "Champions Project" of McCourt, who aimed to return the club to the summit of French soccer and among the European elite when he took over 10 years ago.

The banners read: "2016: Champions Project. 2026: Ligue 2 Project? McCourt Out."

Upon arrival at the vibrant southern port city, McCourt pledged to revive Marseille by investing €200 million ($210 million) over four years. Large amounts of money have since been spent on a myriad of players, without success.

The former Los Angeles Dodgers owner bought Marseille in 2016, and the southern club has struggled to achieve stability.

This summer Marseille failed to qualify for the Champions League after a chaotic season, missing out on millions in revenues. Because of financial constraints, the club did not recruit any new players during the summer transfer window, leaving new coach Bruno Genesio with few options.

Marseille dominated domestic soccer in the late 1980s and early 1990s, but hasn't won the French league title since 2010 and has not claimed a trophy since the now-defunct League Cup in 2012.

The match between Marseille and PSG is still considered the biggest in French soccer despite Marseille's decline in recent years.

Known as "Le Classique," it became popular during the 1990s when the arrival of big stars in the French league ignited a strong rivalry.

But Marseille, the first French team to win the Champions League back in 1993, has fallen well behind since PSG -- now the two-time defending European champion -- were taken over by Qatari investors in 2011.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.
